title: when does buildObject get called?

evidence.author: Martin
evidence.quote: So Cheetah3D knows that it has to update once one of it's childs changes.

evidence.author: Martin
evidence.quote: the setParameter() functions internally calls the buildObject() function to update the scenegraph. So you end in an infinite loop.

evidence.author: Martin
evidence.quote: you can add another boolean parameter which tells if you want to update the scenegraph after you've changed a parameter.

evidence.author: Martin
evidence.quote: sorry that was a bug. For some cases it works for some not.

api_lessons: Call obj.setCreatorObj(true) in buildUI() of a polygon/spline script so buildObject() re-runs when its child objects change.
Calling setParameter() from inside buildObject() triggers a scenegraph update that calls buildObject() again -> infinite loop/hang.
setParameter(name, value, false) - the third boolean argument (added ~3.2, reliable from 3.3) suppresses the scenegraph update.
In 3.x, Tag scripts had no time-change callbacks (placeholder only).
OS.system() runs shell commands; Martin suggested it as a way to offload heavy computation to native command-line tools via files.
notes: Archived code: Martin's buildUI snippet and ToddWR's 'Watch Object' polygon script that hangs because it calls setParameter in buildObject (illustrates the bug, not a working tool).
